**Activity 2 – Define System Component Responsibilities**

| **Component**                        | **Responsibility**                                                                                  | **Input**                                                  | **Output**                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Frontend                             | Displays login, dashboard, customer, order, delivery, payment, rider, route, and<br>deposit screens | User actions and form data.                                | Pages, status messages, tables, and API requests.                                                    |
| Backend                              | Receives API requests and coordinates application functions.                                        | HTTP requests, authenticated user, and submitted data      | Validated results, JSON responses, and database operations. API layer defines endpoints and controls |
| API layer                            | Defines endpoints and controls request/response format.                                             | JSON payloads, URL parameters, and session/token.          | HTTP status codes and JSON data.                                                                     |
| Business logic                       | Applies rules for orders, delivery<br>assignment/status, payments, balances,<br>and deposits.       | Validated records and user role.                           | Approved updates, calculated totals/balances, or validation errors.                                  |
| Database                             | Database Stores and relates the eight proposed<br>entity types                                      | SQL queries and transaction<br>commands.                   | Stored records and query results                                                                     |
| Authentication<br><br>/Authorization | Verifies identity and check's role permissions.                                                     | Login credentials, session/token,<br>and requested action. | Authenticated identity, allowed/denied<br>decision                                                   |
| External services                    | No required third-party integration in initial release; optional<br>map/SMS/payment services later. | Only if an integration is approved<br>and configured.      | Optional route/map data, notifications, or<br>payment confirmation.                                  |

**Activity 3 – Define System Communication and Data Flow**

**Process 1: User registration and login**

| **Required Item**   | **Description**                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Initiator           | Administrator/Owner creates staff or rider accounts; any registered user initiates login.                                                               |
| Receiving component | Frontend sends the request to the backend authentication API.                                                                                           |
| Processing          | Processing                                                                                                                                              |
| Database / service  | MySQL Users/Accounts table (an additional supporting table is proposed because Day 1 did not list user accounts as one of the eight business entities). |
| Response            | Successful login returns a secure session/token and the user's permitted dashboard. Invalid credentials return a generic login error                    |

**Process 2: Customer order creation and delivery assignment**

| **Required Item**   | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Initiator           | Regular User/Staff records a customer's water order.                                                                                                                                 |
| Receiving Component | Frontend sends customer and order details to the backend order API.                                                                                                                  |
| Processing          | Backend validates the customer, gallon type, quantity, price, and availability; calculates the order total; saves the order; then staff/owner assigns a rider and delivery schedule. |
| Database / Service  | MySQL Customer, Order, Gallon, Delivery, Rider, and Route records. The exact foreign-key relationships will be finalized in the database schema.                                     |
| Response            | The frontend displays the saved order number, order summary, and delivery assignment/status.                                                                                         |

**Process 3: Payment recording and balance monitoring**

| **Required Item**   | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Initiator           | Regular User/Staff records a customer payment; the owner may review balances.                                                                                                           |
| Receiving Component | Frontend sends order ID, amount paint, and payment date to the backend payment API.                                                                                                     |
| Processing          | Backend validates the order, validates that the amount is positive and permitted, records the payment, calculates the total paid and remaining balance, and updates the payment status. |
| Database / Service  | MySQL Order and Payment records. Payment history is retained for audit and balance checking                                                                                             |
| Response            | The frontend displays the payment receipt/confirmation and updated outstanding balance.                                                                                                 |

**Process 4: Rider updates delivery status**

| **Required Item**   | **Description**                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Initiator           | Delivery Rider opens an assigned delivery and submits a status update.                                                                        |
| Receiving Component | Frontend sends the update to the backend delivery API.                                                                                        |
| Processing          | Backend confirms the rider is assigned to that delivery, validates the requested status transition, and saves the new status and update time. |
| Database / Service  | MySQL Delivery and Rider records.                                                                                                             |
| Response            | The rider sees the updates status; staff/owner can view the same delivery progress.                                                           |

**Activity 4 – Security Architecture Design**

| **Security Area**   | **Design Decision**                                                                                                               | **Implementation and Explanation**                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Authentication      | Username/email and password login.                                                                                                | Implemented in the backend authentication module. Passwords are checked against salted hashes; failed attempts receive a generic<br>message.                                                                                             |
| Authorization       | Role-based access control (RBAC).                                                                                                 | Backend checks the authenticated role on every protected endpoint.<br>Owner has administrative access; staff can manage permitted customer/order/payment records; riders can view assigned deliveries and<br>update delivery status only |
| Password protection | Use a modern password-hashing algorithm such<br>as Argon2id or bcrypt with a unique salt.                                         | Hashing occurs in the backend before storage. Plain-text passwords are never saved or returned.                                                                                                                                          |
| Data protection     | HTTPS in transit; restricted database access;<br>secrets stored outside source code.                                              | The deployed web server enforces HTTPS. Database credentials are held in environment variables and database accounts receive only required permissions.                                                                                  |
| Input validation    | Validate required fields, formats, lengths, numeric<br>ranges, and allowed values.                                                | Frontend validation improves usability; backend validation is authoritative. Parameterized SQL queries help prevent SQL injection                                                                                                        |
| API security        | HTTPS, authentication on protected routes, role<br>checks, and request validation                                                 | The API layer rejects missing/invalid credentials and unauthorized roles.<br>Do not expose database credentials or internal stack traces                                                                                                 |
| Session management  | Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies for sessions,<br>with expiration and logout; use CSRF protection<br>for cookie-based requests. | Backend creates and invalidates sessions. Sensitive actions require an active session; session cookies are not accessible to browser JavaScript.                                                                                         |
| Error handling      | Consistent user-safe error messages and<br>server-side logs.                                                                      | Backend returns appropriate status codes and a trace/reference ID where<br>useful. Logs must not contain passwords, tokens, or full payment credentials                                                                                  |
| Backup and recovery | Scheduled database backups and tested<br>restoration.                                                                             | Database administrator/owner maintains encrypted backups in a separate secure location. Restore tests are performed periodically; access to<br>backup files is restricted                                                                |

**Activity 5 – Scalability, Performance, and Reliability**

| **Question**                         | **Proposed Answer**                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 1\. What could make the system slow? | Large customer/order/payment tables, unfiltered reports, repeated queries, too many simultaneous requests, slow hosting, and large unoptimized page responses                                                                        |
| 2\. How improve query performance?   | Use joins carefully, select only needed columns, filter and paginate long lists, avoid repeated queries, and<br>inspect slow queries before optimizing.                                                                              |
| 3\. Will indexing be needed?         | Yes. Add indexes to primary keys and frequently searched foreign keys/columns such as Customer_ID,<br>Order_ID, Rider_ID, Delivery_Status, Order_Date, and Payment_Date after checking actual query patterns                         |
| 4\. Multiple users simultaneously?   | Use MySQL transactions for related updates, connection pooling where supported, and backend validation. Transactions help prevent partial payment/order updates and conflicting changes                                              |
| 5\. Support additional modules?      | Keep modules separated (customers, orders, deliveries, payments, inventory/gallons, deposits, reports, users) and expose them through documented API routes                                                                          |
| 6\. External service unavailable?    | The initial release does not depend on external services. If optional SMS/maps/payment integrations are later added, show a clear unavailable message, retry safely where appropriate, and keep core order records available         |
| 7\. Backup and recovery?             | Schedule automatic database backups, retain multiple restore points, store backups separately with restricted access, and test restoration to a separate environment.                                                                |
| 8\. Improvements as system grows?    | Move to a stronger managed database/server, add caching for frequently read data, monitoring, automated tests, a staging environment, and load testing. Consider separating services only when scale justifies the added complexity. |

**Activity 7 – Technical Architecture Decision Record**

| **Decision**             | **Selected Option**                                                                        | **Reason**                                                                                                              | **Alternative Considered**                                                                                               |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Frontend technology      | HTML, CSS, JavaScript                                                                      | Simple, browser-based interface suitable for<br>forms and dashboards                                                    | React or Vue; may be adopted if<br>the interface becomes more<br>complex                                                 |
| Backend technology       | Python Flask                                                                               | Lightweight framework with clear routing and<br>database integration; suitable for a student<br>project.                | Django or Node.js/Express.                                                                                               |
| Database                 | MySQL                                                                                      | Retained from Day 1; relational structure fits customers, orders, deliveries, riders, payments,<br>routes, and deposits | PostgreSQL or SQLite; MySQL<br>remains the selected option                                                               |
| Architectural pattern    | Three-layer architecture<br>(presentation, application/API, data)                          | Separates user interface, business rules, and storage while keeping the initial system<br>manageable                    | Monolithic interface/database<br>coupling or microservices;<br>microservices add unnecessary<br>complexity at this stage |
| Authentication<br>method | Backend login with salted password<br>hashes and role-based access                         | Supports the owner, staff, and rider permissions<br>identified in Day 1.                                                | Third-party identity provider; not<br>required for the initial version.                                                  |
| Hosting/deployment       | Local development initially; deploy<br>web app and MySQL to a secured<br>server when ready | Day 1 did not name a hosting provider. This allows testing before selecting a provider based<br>on cost and reliability | Shared hosting, VPS, or managed<br>cloud hosting; final provider to be<br>decided                                        |
